mcqs.question: Why does structured (JSON) logging scale better than free-text logging as log volume grows?
options: Structured logging removes the need for a buffer or queue stage
Structured logs are always smaller in bytes than free-text logs
Free-text logs cannot be stored in the same system as structured logs
Structured fields can be filtered and aggregated exactly, while free-text logs only support substring or regex search
mcqs.explanation: The scaling advantage is queryability: exact field filters and aggregations versus grep-style substring search. It isn't about file size, storage compatibility, or the pipeline's queueing stage, which are unrelated concerns.

mcqs.question: A service starts logging full request bodies 'for debugging' and a customer's card number ends up in the log store. What's the systemic fix?
options: Scrub or allowlist which fields get logged before they're written, rather than logging raw payloads by default, and review logging code for sensitive-field exposure
Increase log retention so the incident can be reviewed longer
Switch from structured to free-text logging to make the data harder to search
The fix is only to delete that one log line after the fact
mcqs.explanation: The systemic fix is preventing sensitive fields from being logged in the first place via scrubbing/allowlisting and code review -- not increasing retention (which makes exposure worse), changing log format (irrelevant to what's logged), or a one-time deletion that doesn't prevent recurrence.
